clue.text: Alex, say, to undress before artist's sketch

parts.note: to undress is to strip off
a cartoon is a preliminary drawing an artist makes before a painting

explanation.surface: Someone called Alex is told to take their clothes off before sitting for a painter's drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex is a long-running cartoon strip about a City banker, published in the Daily Telegraph itself; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex is one instance of a comic series of panels printed daily in a newspaper.

clue.text: Working hard and investing retained money

indicators.note: retained means the word for investing holds the money inside it

parts.note: investing money is saving it
L stands for pound, the British unit of money (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Someone toils away while putting the cash they kept into investments.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaving means toiling, labouring like a drudge.

clue.text: Called to the bar

definitions.meaning: a crosspiece, as on a ladder

explanation.surface: A barrister being summoned to qualify.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoned someone; and the crosspiece step of a ladder.

clue.text: Colour of US hero of old

parts.note: perse is a dark greyish-blue colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks about the hue of an old American champion.
explanation.walkthrough: PERSE is an old word for a dark blue-grey colour, rare outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Perseus is the Greek mythological slayer of Medusa, a legendary champion.

clue.text: Poisoner to stop using petroleum derivative

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake, so a poisoner
to halt is to stop

explanation.surface: A murderer with poison is asked to give up using oil products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poisoner' looks like a person, but it is the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is a tarry residue left from refining crude oil, used for road surfacing.

clue.text: Neckwear said to be Asian

indicators.note: said signals that the word for neckwear is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a tie is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A remark that a scarf or cravat is reportedly from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE said aloud sounds like THAI; the grid as held prints THAT, an OCR slip for THAI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a person from Thailand, a country of South-East Asia.

clue.text: Reject unpopular actors

parts.note: out means out of favour or fashion
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A director turns down disliked performers.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a person rejected by society, a pariah.

clue.text: Old TV admitting no compromise?

definitions.meaning: early television sets showed no colour
seeing everything as clear-cut, with no grey areas

explanation.surface: An old television set, or an uncompromising attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Monochrome describes old television pictures; and an absolute either-or view of right and wrong.

clue.text: Unsympathetic advice to one in painful labour?

definitions.text: Unsympathetic advice to one in painful labour?

parts.words: Unsympathetic advice to one in painful labour?
parts.note: the stock advice to put up with hardship cheerfully, with a play on bearing a child during labour

explanation.surface: Callous words to a woman giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' reads as childbirth, and 'bear' hints at bearing a child, but the phrase means endure something cheerfully.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells a sufferer to smile and endure trouble without complaint.

clue.text: Student's left a breadwinner

parts.note: a breadwinner is the earner of a household

explanation.surface: A student has abandoned the family wage-earner.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying a subject or skill, as on a driving L-plate.

clue.text: Old colonist put into the earth next to monarch

parts.note: to plant is to set in the ground
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A settler from the past is buried beside a king.
explanation.definitionFit: A planter was a settler in a colony, such as the plantations of Ulster or America.

clue.text: Slice a golf shot

definitions.meaning: a thin piece, as of potato or wood
a short lofted approach onto the green

explanation.surface: A golfer slices a stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin fragment; and a short lofted stroke in golf.

clue.text: Started to request article

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
an is the indefinite article in grammar

explanation.surface: Someone began asking for a newspaper piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Began is the past tense of begin, so it means commenced.

clue.text: Useless to be conceited

definitions.meaning: fruitless, as in a futile attempt

explanation.surface: Being big-headed achieves nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile, as in 'in vain'; and self-admiring.

clue.text: Insinuating ships have capsized

indicators.note: capsized boats are turned upside down, so in this down clue the word for ships is read bottom to top

parts.note: keels, by synecdoche, are ships

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking hint that vessels have overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek can mean smooth and ingratiating in manner, oily.

clue.text: Coach's expression of annoyance with men

parts.note: tut is a sound of disapproval
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, not officers

explanation.surface: A sports trainer sighs crossly at the players.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher, and to coach is to teach or train.

clue.text: Prayer to replace gale with sun

indicators.note: replace asks for the letters of the two words to be put in a new place, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone prays for the storm to give way to sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a substitution, but 'replace' tells you to rearrange GALE and SUN together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion said at morning, noon and evening.

clue.text: Keep taking the mickey in West Country town

parts.note: taking the mickey is British slang for mocking, so taunting
on means continuing, as in 'keep on' or 'carry on'

explanation.surface: Someone goes on teasing people in a town in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: TAUNTON is the county town of Somerset in England's West Country; 'taking the mickey' is British slang for teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunton is the county town of Somerset in south-west England.

clue.text: Volcanic ridge-ship is to get away from the point

indicators.note: volcanic suggests something erupting and thrown about, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A volcanic undersea ridge and a vessel, though the speaker strays off topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volcanic' scrambles RIDGE with SS; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander off the main subject in speech or writing.

clue.text: Through which a beggar sorts?

indicators.note: sorts means the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Rubbish that a tramp rummages through.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines rubbish rummaged through, while 'sorts' rearranges A BEGGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish is what a vagrant might pick through looking for something useful.

clue.text: Crockery may be flying

explanation.surface: Dishes might be thrown across the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Small dishes under teacups; and the flying kind reported as alien craft.

clue.text: Pride swells as one is born

definitions.text: Pride swells as one is born

parts.words: Pride swells as one is born
parts.note: a group of lions, called a pride, gains a member when a youngster arrives

explanation.surface: Someone's pride grows at the birth of a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride' reads as self-satisfaction, but it is the collective noun for lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A young lion is a new member of a lion family group.

clue.text: American soldier is in pub — that's reasonable

indicators.note: in means the soldier is placed inside the word for pub

parts.note: the local is one's nearest or regular pub
GI is a US enlisted soldier

explanation.surface: A US serviceman drinks in a bar, which seems sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: A LOCAL is British slang for one's regular pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical means sensible, following sound reasoning.

clue.text: Fast horse, we hear, is not so well bred

indicators.note: we hear means the word for fast horse is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a courser is a swift horse, a charger

explanation.surface: A swift steed is apparently less refined in breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarser means cruder, less refined in manners.

clue.text: Don't begin magic spell — it causes damage

indicators.note: don't begin tells you to drop the first letter of the word for magic spell

parts.note: a charm is a spell

explanation.surface: Warning someone not to start casting a spell, since it does harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm is injury or hurt.

clue.text: Quietly press to clear out

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to urge is to press someone

explanation.surface: Gently pushing someone to tidy up.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to rid or cleanse of unwanted things.

clue.text: Soldier writing a few lines

definitions.meaning: a short abbreviated name for a section of text

explanation.surface: A serviceman writes a short note.
explanation.definitionFit: A paratrooper; and short for paragraph, a few sentences of text.

clue.text: Not quite wonderful North European

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter of the word for wonderful is dropped

parts.note: fine means excellent

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian is described as only nearly great.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn is a native of Finland, in northern Europe.

clue.text: Announce liberal arrested for murder

indicators.note: arrested means the word for announce holds the liberal inside it

parts.note: to say is to announce
L stands for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: A newsreader reports a Liberal politician held on a killing charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To slay is to kill violently.

clue.text: Period to eat in? Yes!

parts.note: a time of day for a meal, the exclamation confirming the meal is literally named in it

explanation.surface: A question about when to eat, answered emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: The late-afternoon hour for a cup and a snack is a time of day for eating.

clue.text: Firm has deficit, one making huge figures

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
a loss is a shortfall
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A company in the red makes enormous statues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' reads as accounts, but means statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi are gigantic statues, like the ancient one at Rhodes.

clue.text: Steffi, say, earns plenty — I must struggle

indicators.note: struggle suggests the letters writhing about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rich sports star admits the speaker has to fight hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Steffi Graf was a German champion of the women's game in the 1980s and 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf is an example of a famous champion of the racket sport.
